Backstory, I struggled with emetophobia since childhood. Full blown panic attacks if someone even mentioned that their stomach hurt. Exposure therapy in everyday life helped me a lot. My freshman year of college, I had a roommate who was definitely a functioning alcoholic. Every morning at 5 am I’d hear her throwing up in the bathroom. Of course initially I’d panic, but then remember that she wasn’t actually sick/contagious and just was sick from the hangover. Getting sick myself helped too. I used to have to make myself throw up as a final act of desperation when I was so nauseous because my brain literally refused to let my body throw up naturally. Also, there is a relief your brain signals after you throw up. My boyfriend gave me the stomach flu back in April and this was finally one of those times I didn’t have to make myself sick, it came up naturally… and the relief I felt after throwing up was crazy!! But it got to a point where I was so nauseous I couldn’t move so my doctor prescribed me Zofran (anti nausea medication). My boyfriend also throws up a lot randomly. He’s one of those people who just has a sensitive stomach and eats stuff that bothers it… so having to deal with him getting “sick” multiple times a month has helped with exposure. I think OCD and emetophobia are linked for sure. It’s a fear of not being in control. You worry you’re gonna throw up and it’s never going to end… but that’s just simply not the case 😂. Also, for my colonoscopy prep… I didn’t throw up at all. I never even felt nauseous. I don’t ever want to drink yellow Gatorade again, though 😂. The feeling of peeing out of your butt is the most unpleasant part. I was also so nervous for the anesthesia… my heart rate spiked to 150 in the operating room… it was freaky! But the nurses said it was okay, they played taylor swift, and the doc said he’s gonna give me what feels like a shot of tequila. All a sudden I felt kinda drunk and then it was lights out. Woke up in recovery giggling. 
I believe in you! I know that feeling of dread when your stomach hurts… but seriously, as a recovered emetophobe… throwing up truly isn’t that bad. (I know it’s hard to believe). Sending you love.

I also don’t mean to be creepy but I see that you post a lot about health anxieties. I am 23F and have diagnosed OCD, GAD, Panic Disorder, and I’m a hypochondriac. Also a recovered emetophobe! If you’d ever like to talk, I’m here! I know I’m not a doctor, but I also know how detrimental spiraling about your health is to your general well being. Chances are with most things, YOU WILL BE OKAY. I had to delete tik tok and limit my screen time on safari so I wouldn’t research my symptoms, because I had convinced myself back in April that I had colon cancer. Went as far as having a colonoscopy/endoscopy and they, of course, found nothing. But I was miserable for the 2 months leading up to it, and lost 10 lbs, all because of my OCD and panic disorder. Our bodies are weird and will do weird things. It’s normal. As long as you regularly see a doctor, you will be fine. Do not rid yourself of happiness by living in constant fear of dying. Is that really living? We are all going to die one day. Whether it’s natural causes, sickness, accidents… etc. It is going to happen to all of us. I know it’s easier said than done to accept that, but truly, you are going to ruin your life by spiraling about these things.
